rationale: The hypothesis posits that isolated fetal horseshoe kidney (HSK) represents an ultra-rare presentation of PSMD12 variants (~1-2% prevalence in isolated fetal HSK cohorts) and that these individuals invariably manifest neurodevelopmental delay (NDD) or craniofacial dysmorphism postnatally rather than maintaining isolated renal anomalies. Exome sequencing of CMA-negative isolated fetal HSK by Yu et al. (2026) identified a pathogenic PSMD12 splicing variant (c.796-1G>A) in 1 of 45 exome-sequenced cases (2.2%) and 1 of 95 total isolated HSK cases (1.05%), matching the ~1-2% prevalence estimate. Extensive phenotypic profiling of Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome across all published cohorts (Küry et al. 2017, Isidor et al. 2022, Feresin et al. 2025) demonstrates 100% penetrance for developmental delay/intellectual disability and craniofacial dysmorphism across both de novo and inherited familial truncating variants, with no reported individuals possessing isolated renal anomalies or non-penetrant neurodevelopmental phenotypes. A key limitation is that the single fetal HSK case identified by Yu et al. was terminated prenatally, precluding direct postnatal longitudinal observation of that specific case; however, complete clinical penetrance in all established postnatal cohorts strongly supports the hypothesis.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 95 fetuses presenting with isolated horseshoe kidney on second-trimester ultrasound, chromosomal microarray analysis followed by trio exome sequencing in 45 CMA-negative cases identified a pathogenic splicing variant in PSMD12 (c.796-1G>A) in 1 fetus (2.2% of sequenced, 1.05% of the total cohort). The pregnancy was terminated following diagnosis.

source.title: Clinically Significant Genetic Results in Fetuses With Isolated Horseshoe Kidney
source.quote: Among the cases that yielded negative results from CMA, 45 proceeded to trio ES. Notably, two disease-causing variants, c.796-1G > A in PSMD12 and c.11707 C > T (p.Gln3903*) in KMT2D, were detected in each case. Three pregnancies affected by CNVs along with a PSMD12 variant were terminated upon parental decision‐making.

evidence.text: Characterization of 24 unrelated patients with Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome caused by PSMD12 haploinsufficiency confirmed full penetrance of neurodevelopmental phenotypes (developmental delay/intellectual disability and speech delay) alongside craniofacial dysmorphism and variable systemic anomalies including renal, cardiac, and skeletal malformations.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: Haploinsufficiency of PSMD12 has been reported in individuals with neurodevelopmental phenotypes, including developmental delay/intellectual disability (DD/ID), facial dysmorphism, and congenital malformations, defined as Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (STISS)... In addition to previously reported DD/ID, speech delay, cardiac and renal anomalies, we also confirmed preaxial hand abnormalities as a feature of this syndrome.

evidence.text: Evaluation of six individuals across two generations harboring truncating PSMD12 variants demonstrated complete penetrance with developmental delay, intellectual disability, craniofacial dysmorphisms, and skeletal anomalies in 100% (6/6) of cases, showing no individuals with isolated anomalies or non-penetrant neurological phenotypes.

source.title: Does It Run in Your Family? Inherited Truncating  PSMD12  Variants Broaden the Phenotypic Spectrum of Stankiewicz‐Isidor Syndrome
source.quote: Portraying a completely penetrant condition with inter- and intra-familiar clinical variability, all individuals presented with developmental delay, intellectual disability, craniofacial, and skeletal anomalies.

evidence.text: Discovery and functional characterization of de novo truncating and splice-site variants in PSMD12 in individuals with syndromic neurodevelopmental disorders confirmed that proteasome 26S non-ATPase subunit 12 haploinsufficiency underlies syndromic intellectual disability rather than isolated congenital structural anomalies.

source.title: De novo disruption of the proteasome regulatory subunit PSMD12 causes a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder

evidence.text: Evaluation of 515 patients with CAKUT (500 syndromic/CAKUT+ and 15 isolated CAKUT) demonstrated that monogenic causes of CAKUT frequently present with syndromic neurodevelopmental disorders (e.g., ADNP, PHIP, SETD5), highlighting that genes causing structural kidney malformations often overlap with systemic neurodevelopmental syndromes rather than isolated urogenital disease.

source.title: Clinical exome sequencing efficacy and phenotypic ... - PMC
source.quote: We determined that cES established a molecular diagnosis in 27.4% (141/515) of individuals in this cohort... These findings lead us to conclude that cES should be considered in individuals with CAKUT+ for whom a molecular diagnosis has not been identified... and that individuals with ADNP-, PHIP-, and SETD5-related disorders may present with CAKUT phenotypes.

conflicts: Direct postnatal confirmation of neurodevelopmental delay and craniofacial dysmorphism in the isolated fetal horseshoe kidney case was precluded because the pregnancy was terminated upon molecular diagnosis.

Isolated prenatal presentation may reflect the limitation of second-trimester ultrasound in detecting subtle craniofacial dysmorphism or predicting cognitive/developmental trajectory rather than a true biological restriction of the pathology to renal tissue.

new_directions.question_text: In ongoing prospective cohorts of prenatally diagnosed isolated CAKUT/horseshoe kidney undergoing exome sequencing, what percentage of pregnancies carried to term manifest neurodevelopmental delay or minor dysmorphisms during early childhood?
new_directions.rationale: Directly resolves whether prenatally 'isolated' structural kidney anomalies carrying PSMD12 loss-of-function variants invariably show full penetrance for neurodevelopmental delay postnatally without the confounding factor of elective termination.

new_directions.question_text: What is the molecular and cellular mechanism by which proteasomal subunit PSMD12 haploinsufficiency disrupts metanephric mesenchyme migration and ureteric bud branching to cause horseshoe kidney?
new_directions.rationale: Understanding the developmental timing and cell-type specificity of PSMD12 expression in the developing renal blastema versus the neuroepithelium will explain why fusion defects (horseshoe kidney) occur in only a subset of syndromic STISS patients.
